page_hint: Ch 26 §3 Pattern A; Ch 26 §8 Capstone Step 1; Appendix A §5
quoted_clause: can hold ~17.5 concurrent 9,500-token requests within the canonical ~436 GB KV budget
it is *not* the canonical 9.2K-input/1.08-s-prefill case of Ch 4
The book's canonical scenario is a 70B dense FP16, ~9.2K-token RAG workload on 8×H100
observed: The canonical RAG input length is stated as 9,500 tokens in Pattern A (where 17.5 concurrent requests and the ~2.0 req/s per-host ceiling are derived) but as ~9.2K (9,200) in the same chapter's capstone and in Appendix A §5. These are distinct values, not a rounding variant (9.5K ≠ 9.2K).
evidence: Recompute concurrent capacity: 436×10⁹ B ÷ (2.62×10⁶ B/token × 9,500 tokens) = 17.52 ≈ 17.5 (matches printed). With 9,200 tokens: 436×10⁹ ÷ (2.62×10⁶ × 9,200) = 18.09 ≈ 18.1 (does not match printed 17.5). Per-host ceiling: 17.5 / 8.6 s = 2.035 ≈ 2.0 (matches); 18.1 / 8.6 = 2.10 (would print as ~2.1, not ~2.0). The 17.5 and 2.0 figures are locked to 9,500, not 9,200.
root_cause: One of the two canonical input-length values (9,500 or 9.2K) is stale. All derived quantities in this chunk (17.5 concurrent, 2.0 req/s, 8.6 s service) are consistent with 9,500. The 9.2K references in the capstone and Appendix A were not updated (or vice versa).
correction: Unify to a single canonical input length across Ch 26 and Appendix A. If 9,500 is the correct value, change the capstone's '9.2K-input' to '9.5K-input' and Appendix A §5's '~9.2K-token' to '~9.5K-token'. If 9,200 is correct, recompute 17.5 → ~18.1 and 2.0 → ~2.1 throughout.
acceptance_test: Every reference to the canonical RAG input length in Ch 26 (Pattern A, Capstone Step 1) and Appendix A (§5) states the same numeric value, and the 17.5-concurrent / 2.0-req/s derivation is arithmetically consistent with that value (436 GB ÷ (2.62 MB/token × L) ≈ 17.5 and 17.5 ÷ 8.6 s ≈ 2.0).

quoted_clause: Hybrid-attention models cut it 4–10× at the mechanism in the named configurations — a band across models, not a universal constant
observed: The '4–10×' band mixes two different scopes and omits a stated total-KV figure. The 4.4× lower bound is GLM's per-layer KV reduction, which the text explicitly disclaims as 'not whole-model FLOP or total-cache ratios.' The stated total-KV reductions are ~10× (DeepSeek V4-Pro, ~10% of V3.2) and ~14× (DeepSeek V4-Flash, ~7% of V3.2). The band should be 10–14× for total KV, or the per-layer 4.4× should be presented separately.
evidence: DeepSeek §1: '~10% / ~7% of its KV cache' → 1/0.10 = 10× and 1/0.07 ≈ 14.3×. GLM §4: '4.4× smaller KV cache. These are not whole-model FLOP or total-cache ratios.' The 4.4× is per-head-per-layer; the 10× and ~14× are total. The printed band '4–10×' includes the per-layer 4.4× and the total 10× but excludes the total ~14×.
root_cause: The band was assembled from the minimum cited number (4.4×, per-layer) and a subset of the maximum (10×, total) without separating per-layer from total scope, and without including the ~14× Flash total figure.
correction: Rewrite as: 'Hybrid-attention models cut total per-token KV by 10–14× in the named configurations (DeepSeek V4-Pro ~10×, V4-Flash ~14×); GLM-5.3-Flash reports a 4.4× per-layer reduction (not a total-cache ratio). These are a band across models and scopes, not a universal constant.'
acceptance_test: The stated reduction band covers every total-KV figure cited in the appendix (10× and ~14×), per-layer figures are explicitly labeled as such and not mixed into the total band, and no cited total-KV reduction falls outside the stated range.
